posts.name: Paul
posts.cooked:
1) That is correct.

2) Since Tactics was released, the board game market has changed significantly. Going forward, Prime War products will include the miniatures in the box.

3) They are going to be somewhat different. Most notably, they will have a different sort of base and the sculpts will be better, more in line with the kind of miniatures we released with Fate of the Elder Gods.

4) I assume you mean easy to get the Sentinel Tactics miniatures? If so, yes! They are available for 50% off MSRP on our web store right now.

5) Before Prime War ships, we'll make an announcement that address changes are needed, and have you email us your new address.

6) The map tiles for sure, as well as the hex tokens for the characters (if you don't have the Flame of Freedom/Uprising miniatures).

7) We definitely hope to! We'll see how the connection is in the expo center; that's always the trouble with Gen Con streaming. The Letters Page and the like are all in attached hotels, so it is easier.

8) If you pre-ordered Broken City (without miniatures) and want to upgrade to a with-miniatures version, it will be the same price as if you had ordered miniatures with your Broken City preorder in the first place.

9) Possibly. As I mentioned earlier, the Tactics miniatures are already 50% off on our web store, and we intend to keep them there at that heavy discount.

10) Yes, but the details are a Christopher / Letters Page question.

11) Possibly at some point.

12) The gameplay is far ahead of the art, but he'll tease some once he has some to tease.

13) We'll go into more gameplay details at Gen Con and during our livestreams this fall.

Spiff:

The paragraph about how Prime War fits into the Sentinels story seems unnecessarily convoluted to me.  It says the Prime Aspects can draw champions from multiple realities, but there are only two realities left, Sentinels and Mist Storm.  Are we saying there are more realities than those now?  If there are more now, why bother to say that they're going to draw from Mist Storm first?  If they can pull from multiple realities, then it's a straighter line to just say they pulled the characters from multiple realities.  If you have to explain the failed Mist Storm universe to someone when trying to explain the Prime Wars universe, you're just complicating things for no good reason.  This story needs a little more editorial trimming, IMO.

Yes, there are and have always been more than those two.  Those are the two in which Sentinel Comics took place (not counting Disparation), but very few alternate realities were completely destroyed.

I assume they're pulling from Mist Storm because 1) the core products' characters will come from there, 2) the Mist Storm universe is what used to be the Tactics universe, and they want to create continuity, and 3) the Mist Storm universe is fully fleshed out, so it's positioned well to be the "default".  They probably added in Disparation because it polled well and because Haka made no sense otherwise.

My biggest question is how long the game takes to set up.  That's the main reason my group barely touched Tactics.

posts.cooked:
I am glad to see that the current plan is to include a co-operative mode. IMO this aspect was a hallmark of Sentinels of the Multiverse and I was disappointed it hadn't carried over to Sentinel Tactics. More recently I have enjoyed playing co-op mini games such as Star Wars Imperial Assault, Mansions of Madness, and Shadows of Brimstone, so I look forward to hearing more about this aspect.
 
Some questions...
 
#1 - The original Kickstarter for Sentinel Tactics had the map pack add-ons which were to include scenarios. I understand the scenarios are currently being reworked for the new Prime War, but what compensation will be offered to customers who are not getting Prime War and have not had their original Kickstarter 100% fulfilled due to the missing scenarios?
 

#2 - Previously the status of Battle for Broken City and For Profit, and then Sentinel Tactics Wave 2 Prime War and Rise of the Ennead have been marked by a lack of transparency in the development process and delays, especially when compared to your other campaigns and products. What kind of transparency can we expect in the development of the current Prime War line, specifically in gameplay, and updates and delays to the projected delivery date?
 

#3 - Are there any plans to incorporate app interfaces for tablets and computer, like Star Wars Imperial Assault and Mansions of Madness do?

 

Thank you.

posts.name: Spiff
posts.cooked:
Powerhound_2000:

Multiple Realities didn’t go away they just can’t be traversed any of at all by the heroes/villains post OblivAeon

Got it.  However, I'm going to continue my opinion-giving by saying that I've always thought the Mist Storm universe was an awkward bolt-on that ran counter to the clean narrative of the end of the Multiverse.

"… and then the heroes defeated OblivAeon and in doing so, the pathways to the other universes were shut forever" is a clean ending to a clean narrative.  But GtG needed reasons for heroes and villains to fight each other in a tactical game that wasn't compatible with the world they envisioned for their RPG so they didn't stop with the clean ending.  Instead they said:

"… BUT!  There's this one other universe that's gritty and dark where everyone fights everyone else.  So there isn't just one accessible universe, there are two for… reasons."

My point here is that Tactics failed and the universe created to support it isn't necessary.  I think it should just be retconned away to keep the narrative clean.  If the narrative were:

"… but those other universes are still out there and when the Prime Aspects needed champions for their war, they drew them from the myriad of realities they alone could access", that's reasonably clean.  No Mist Storm needed.  Don't make anyone have to explain the Mist Storm universe to their friends when they're describing Prime War because it will only make people say "yeah, the Mist Storm universe was this thing from Tactics, which you've never heard of because no one wanted to play it so they invented this game instead."  I'm just saying, keep it clean.

Prime War sounds much less compatible with the original Tactics than I thought it would be. (Somehow I figured all the components, dice, etc would be the same and all we’d need is a new rule sheet.) However, I do have to say that the action selection mechanism seems like it would create a much smoother game flow than the original phases.

I’m pleased to see that there will be a cooperative mode, players vs the game! I really hope that mode works well. I am very curious how the automated villains will handle movement and targeting. The automation schemes for games like Scythe always seem so clunky to me.
